cells.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from using coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley, and vendors are prohibited from selling, licensing, or providing such algorithms to Berkeley landlords.

Landlords are prohibited from asking about, advertising, or using criminal history in rental housing applications, tenant selection, or decision-making, and cannot charge higher rent or security deposits based on criminal history, with specific exemptions such as owner-occupied properties with 1-3 units.

Landlords evicting tenants for an owner move-in or under the Ellis Act must pay a standard relocation assistance payment of $19,413, plus an additional $6,471 for qualifying households. Additionally, landlords may not evict for nonpayment unless rental debt equals or exceeds one month's Fair Market Rent.

Landlords cannot charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy or manage roommates, and when charging screening fees, must provide a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement along with the maximum fee cap permitted under state law.

The maximum tenant screening fee a landlord can charge a prospective tenant is capped at $68.96 for 2026 (or alternatively up to $30 adjustable by CPI under Civil Code 1950.6), and landlords cannot charge a fee if no unit is available.
cells.conflict_note: Members 8/9 state $68.96 for 2026 while members 51/52 state a $30 limit adjustable by CPI.

cells.requirement: Landlords may only charge up to one month's rent as a security deposit, except certain small landlords who may charge up to two months' rent. Deposits must be returned within 21 days with an itemized statement of deductions.

Landlords in units covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance must pay tenants interest on their security deposits annually and prorated upon move-out, and are otherwise bound by state-level security deposit limits and return timelines.

Eligible landlords may increase permanent rent ceilings by up to 1.0% for 2026, while the general Annual General Adjustment cap is 5%. Pre-1980 multifamily units are subject to rent control, with specific exemptions for new construction and certain single-family homes.

Housing providers are prohibited from discriminating against protected characteristics and source of income, and cannot use blanket bans on criminal history or consider non-conviction records, sealed files, or juvenile matters.

It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce, or to coerce another person to set or adopt recommended prices or commercial terms.

After 12 months of continuous occupancy, landlords may not terminate a residential tenancy without just cause stated in the written notice, and no-fault evictions require relocation assistance equal to one month's rent.
Landlords are prohibited from increasing gross rental rates by more than 5 percent plus the cost of living change, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period.
cells.key_value: 5% plus cost of living change or 10% lower limit

cells.requirement: The City Council instructed the Los Angeles Housing Department to report on the use of algorithm-based software for establishing rents and the feasibility of instituting a ban.

Landlords are prohibited from terminating tenancies without just cause and must provide relocation assistance for no-fault evictions. Tenants cannot be evicted for nonpayment unless unpaid rent exceeds the Fair Market Rent.

Annual rent increases for RSO units are set to 3% from July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026, and beginning February 2, 2026, landlords can no longer include additional percentage increases for utilities.
Landlords are prohibited from terminating a residential tenancy without just cause, categorized into at-fault and no-fault reasons.
Proposed ordinance making it unlawful for any person to provide an algorithmic rent-setting device to a landlord, or for a landlord to use such a device to set rental rates or occupancy levels.
cells.key_value: civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation

cells.requirement: Landlords must have one of 17 permitted just cause reasons to evict a tenant from a covered unit, and must pay prescribed relocation payments for no-fault evictions like owner move-ins or Ellis Act withdrawals.
The annual allowable rent increase for rent-controlled units is set to 1.6% from March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027.
Landlords are prohibited from selling or using software or algorithmic devices that analyze nonpublic competitor rental data to set rent prices or manage occupancy levels.
Landlords must pay interest on security deposits at the rate of 4.2% for the period from March 1, 2026 to February 28, 2027.
Annual rent increases are capped at the lower of 3% or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change over the most recent 12-month period.
cells.key_value: 3% or 80% of CPI change, whichever is less

cells.requirement: Landlords must have a valid just cause reason to terminate a tenancy and must provide 3 months of relocation assistance (or waive the final 3 months of rent) for no-fault evictions.
